key_prerequisites.name: The Nth Term Test for Divergence

sections.normalized_html:
Which of the following series converge?

  1. [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{e^{2n}}{n^{99}}]

  2. [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{\ln(2n+1)}{n}]

  3. [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{4^n}{n!}]
sections.readable_text:
Which of the following series converge?

1. [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{e^{2n}}{n^{99}}]
2. [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{\ln(2n+1)}{n}]
3. [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{4^n}{n!}]

sections.normalized_html:
We use the flowchart below to determine which tests to use for each series.

With that in mind, let's test each series in turn.

  • For the first series, we use the [MATH: n]th term test for divergence. Let [MATH: a_n= \dfrac{e^{2n}}{n^{99}}.] Then, we have [MATH: \displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}a_n=\infty,] since the exponential term in the numerator grows faster than the polynomial in the denominator. Therefore, by the [MATH: n]th term test, the series [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{e^{2n}}{n^{99}}] is divergent.

  • For the second series, we use the comparison test. Observe that [MATH: \ln (2n + 1) > 1⟹(\ln (2n + 1))/(n) > (1)/(n)] for all [MATH: n\geq 1.] Now, the series [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{1}{n}] is divergent by the [MATH: p]-series test. So, by the comparison test, the series [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty \dfrac{\ln(2n+1)}{n}] is also divergent.

  • For the final series, we use the ratio test. Let [MATH: a_n= \dfrac{4^n}{n!}.] Working out the necessary limit, we get [MATH: L|= lim_(n → ∞)|(a_{n + 1})/(a_{n})|; = lim_(n → ∞)((4^{n + 1})/((n + 1)!) ÷ (4^{n})/(n!)); = lim_(n → ∞)((4^{n + 1})/((n + 1)!) ⋅ (n!)/(4^{n})); = lim_(n → ∞)((4(4^{n}))/(n!(n + 1)) ⋅ (n!)/(4^{n})); = lim_(n → ∞)((4(4^{n}))/(n!(n + 1)) ⋅ (n!)/(4^{n})); = lim_(n → ∞)((4)/(n + 1)); = 0.] Since [MATH: L=0 < 1,] we conclude that the series is convergent.

In conclusion, only series III converges.

items.title: Identifying True Statements About Infinite Series

sections.normalized_html:
If the series [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n] is convergent and [MATH: a_n] is a positive, strictly decreasing sequence for all [MATH: n\geq 1,] then which of the following statements must be true?

  1. Given that [MATH: f(n) = a_n,] where [MATH: f(x)] is continuous and strictly decreasing, then [MATH: \displaystyle\int_1^\infty f(x)\,\textrm d x] converges.

  2. [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^n a_n] is convergent.

  3. [MATH: \displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left| \dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right| = 1.]
sections.readable_text:
If the series [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n] is convergent and [MATH: a_n] is a positive, strictly decreasing sequence for all [MATH: n\geq 1,] then which of the following statements must be true?

1. Given that [MATH: f(n) = a_n,] where [MATH: f(x)] is continuous and strictly decreasing, then [MATH: \displaystyle\int_1^\infty f(x)\,\textrm d x] converges.
2. [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^n a_n] is convergent.
3. [MATH: \displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left| \dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right| = 1.]

sections.normalized_html:
Let's analyze each statement.

  • Statement I is true. The sequence [MATH: a_n] and the function [MATH: f(x)] satisfy the conditions for the integral test. According to the integral test, since [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n] is convergent, then [MATH: \displaystyle\int_1^\infty f(x)\,\textrm d x] is convergent.

  • Statement II is true. Since [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n] is convergent, we must have that [MATH: \displaystyle \lim_{n\to\infty}a_n = 0.] By the alternating series test, then, [MATH: \displaystyle \sum_{n=1}^\infty (-1)^n a_n] is convergent.

  • Statement III is false. Recall that with the ratio test, [MATH: L = \displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left| \dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right| = 1] gives no conclusion as to whether the series converges or diverges. In other words, there exist convergent series with [MATH: L=1.]

In conclusion, only statements I and II must be true.
